title: Seattle, Nepal, and Everywhere In Between: A Year of Milestones and Memories

content.text: At the start of the year, we welcomed an incredible new addition to our family: Kashiv Dahal. From the moment he arrived, Kashiv has been a bundle of pure joy. Following tradition, his Nwaran ceremony was held 10 days after his birth, where his name was officially finalized as Kashiv Dahal.

Even before Kashiv was born, my mom was with us, helping Karuna prepare for his arrival. After his birth, while Karuna was recovering and Kashiv was busy figuring out life (literally), Mom and I took some time to explore the Bay Area. From Cal State East Bay to Napa Valley, we mapped it all out. It was a fun time, and her company made it even more enjoyable.

When Maghe Sakranti arrived, it was especially meaningful this year, as we celebrated it with Kashiv as part of our growing family. I even tried my hand at making til laddoo for the first time, and it turned out delicious! A big thanks to Krishna Bhinaju for the guidance and to my mom for her mentorship—I couldn’t have done it without them.s

As Kashiv grew, he started making little noises that brought joy to everyone. We celebrated with family, took photos, and even enjoyed a barbecue. Later, we celebrated Karuna’s birthday (aka Kashiv’s mom). I won’t say how many years she turned, but let’s just say it was a fun celebration. 😆

After spending a few months with Kashiv and family, it was time for a big move. My job relocated from San Francisco to Seattle, so I packed up and, with Krishna Bhinaju riding shotgun, we embarked on the journey. Our first stop was Mount Shasta, where the mountain showcased its stunning beauty in springtime. Next, we visited the tulip fields in Woodburn, Oregon, and then Multnomah Falls—a breathtakingly large waterfall that slimmed down to a horsetail shape during drier months.

Finally, we reached my new apartment in University Village, Seattle. The sunny welcome was an unexpected but much-appreciated surprise, lifting my spirits after the long journey. I dropped Krishna Bhinaju at the airport, and I can't fully express how grateful I am for all his unwavering support throughout the move. From helping with packing to offering advice every step of the way, his presence made everything smoother. I thanked him deeply, but it still feels like I can never truly convey how much his kindness and guidance meant to me.

Living alone in Seattle felt like the opening scene of a movie. The city’s beauty, the warmth of its people, and the collective joy everyone shares when the sun shines made it easier to settle in. I even set up a projector to create my own little entertainment system. But, as anyone who's lived alone knows, there can be moments of loneliness. To find balance, I turned to hiking. My first solo hike at Innis Arden Reserve Park sparked a newfound love for the outdoors. I quickly joined hiking groups and ventured out on more trails, including Poo Poo Point (where the views were underwhelming, but the company was great) and Rattlesnake Ledge, where the fresh air and breathtaking scenery felt nothing short of magical.

A highlight of the year was flying back to California to attend Kashiv’s Annaprashana. Despite my initial fear of flying on a 737-Max (which had a troubling history), the excitement of seeing Kashiv, now a 6-month-old, made it all worth it. The ceremony was a grand affair, with over 80 dishes prepared, and Kashiv got to sample some of them. Relatives and friends from around the world, including Nanish and Anamol from Texas, joined in the celebration. Afterward, we enjoyed a family barbecue and even took a trip to Sacramento. Thank you Nanish and Anamol for making the trip to bless Kashiv 😊

Returning to Seattle, I dove deeper into hiking, embracing both the challenges and the rewards it brought. One of the most demanding hikes was Mailbox Peak. It tested our limits—our group encountered some emergencies along the way, but we made it to the top, creating unforgettable memories despite the obstacles. After that intense experience, I sought out easier trails to regain my balance. I hiked Cherry Creek Falls, a relatively short trek, but the serenity it offered made it worthwhile. Then came Lake Serene—a true highlight. The lake’s calm waters and breathtaking surroundings lived up to its name, and the beauty of the hike left me feeling more connected to nature than ever.

I was beyond excited—so excited, in fact, that I shared my fun-filled experiences with my friends, and they couldn’t wait to join me. Sahaj was the first to make the trip. On our first day, we visited the Amazon Spheres, the Space Needle, Pike Place Market, and the Seattle Aquarium. Quick tip for anyone planning to visit Pike Place Market: bring chewing gum! There’s a wall covered in used gum, and it smells exactly like dried chewing gum. I was shocked, surprised, excited, and disgusted all at once—definitely a rare combination of feelings.

To make the most of the outdoor adventures, Sahaj and I went hiking to Rattlesnake, Agnes Lake, and Mount Rainier—all in three days. It was a blast, but a heads-up for anyone planning to visit Mount Rainier: go after 3 p.m. or book an appointment. Sahaj was lucky enough to miss the almost-top part of the mountain. That luck followed us to Portland, where construction on I-5 made it impossible to reach the city on time, and we ended up missing Multnomah Falls. Sahaj took advantage of Oregon’s no state tax and did some shopping, and we caught up with an old coworker. Then we stayed in the sketchiest motel I’ve ever seen. Early one morning, someone knocked on our door, looking like he was there to collect blood. I was terrified, but Sahaj slept through it like a rock—some people are made of steel.

After almost getting killed in the motel, we went to Multnomah Falls, but there was no parking. We couldn’t find a spot, so we ended up visiting Horseshoe Bend for some pictures. By then, I was starting to think I wasn’t that lucky, though I realized there were people more unlucky than me. We finally caved and paid for parking to visit Multnomah Falls, but, of course, the water had dried up because it was mid-summer. Sahaj definitely brought that DC energy!

After spending a week with Sahaj, a friend from school, Asim came to visit me. It was great catching up with him, and we spent a couple of hours reminiscing about our childhood memories. Thanks again, mate, and all the best with your master’s degree!
After hanging out with some cool people, I was back at work, and let me tell you—it was a wild experience. Now I truly understand the importance of staying grounded.

A few days later, Prabin came to Seattle for a visit. We revisited all the spots I had seen with Sahaj, but since Prabin had more time, we also explored Bellevue. We checked out Microsoft and some of the beautiful lakes in the area. We even went to Discovery Park, though it was raining that day, and Prabin—coming from Houston—was pretty shocked by the weather. But there was one bright spot: Prabin managed to take some great photos! Not that I’m saying he’s a pro photographer 😂, but the pictures turned out really well.

Prabin and I went on some interesting hikes, starting with Rattlesnake, and then immediately stepping it up with Granite Falls. Looking back, going to Granite Falls was a pretty terrible decision. We started the hike around 7 p.m. and ended up arriving at night, which made it feel risky—at one point, I seriously thought we were doomed or lost. But with good company, we eventually made it to the right place. That night, we had Indian-style pizza, which wasn’t great, but hey, it was my first time trying it!

Taking our bad decisions to the next level, we decided to hike Mount Pilchuck on a rainy day. Yes, Mount Pilchuck in the rain. Armed with our ponchos, we thought, “What could stop us?” Apparently, everything. It was freezing, slippery, and there was no view at the top. I even lost my hairband! At one point, it was so cold at the summit that we were only in t-shirts, proving that Nepalese aren’t scared of anything. Was it worth it? The views—no. But the memory was definitely top-tier. Huge thanks to Prabin for being the best company through it all.

How could we top that? Well, we decided to go to Port Angeles and hike Mount Storm King. Now, remember, Prabin’s shoes were wet, so like responsible adults, we used a hair dryer to dry them out. Don’t let the name Mount Storm King fool you—while it sounded cool, the hike was insane. We gained about 4,000 feet in just 2 hours, and at the top, we needed to rope climb to get up. It was risky, to say the least. And the descent? Jesus, I’m just glad we made it out alive.

After so many risky adventures, we decided to do something safer and went to Portland. We visited a couple of places I had already been with Sahaj, and of course, Prabin took advantage of Oregon’s no sales tax.

Finally, we made our way to Mount Rainier. It was crazy cold when we arrived, and we got there early because the gates didn’t open until after 3 p.m. We spent almost an hour just counting cars and predicting what would come next. After the wait, we finally hiked Mount Rainier, covering all the popular trails. The hike was great, and Prabin’s company made it even better. After that, Prabin had to head back to Houston to continue his life and, I’m sure, more hiking. Houston, of all places! After the trip, I was so motivated that I decided to hike Mt. Si alone, which had almost 4,500 feet of elevation gain. I was completely drenched after the climb, but it felt amazing.

Then came the big trip of the year—I went to Nepal. It would have been a simple journey if I’d flown directly from the U.S. to Nepal, but no, there were multiple transits involved. First, I flew from Seattle to Doha, then to Delhi, and finally to Kathmandu. The flight to Delhi was smooth, but my next flight was with Nepal Airlines. I landed at 2 a.m. and had about 12 hours to explore Delhi. But, of course, Nepal Airlines had other plans and moved my flight from 4 p.m. to midnight the next day. So, there I was, sleepless in Delhi. Despite having virtually no sleep in the last 72 hours, I toured the city, visiting all the major attractions like Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Chandni Chowk, India Gate, and more. It was hectic, and let me tell you, Chandni Chowk is something else in real life—it definitely needs some humanitarian help! I ate all the best food and saw all the sights. By midday, I was beyond drowsy and could’ve slept anywhere, but I resisted. Finally, I boarded the Nepal Airlines flight at 11:06 p.m., and the moment I closed my eyes, I was out. The next thing I remember is landing—I have no idea what happened in between!

Arriving in Nepal was amazing. I was welcomed with Hajurbua’s famous popcorn and Nepal’s delicious chats. And yes, I made sure to eat the momos—they tasted exactly as I remembered: perfect. Dashain came, and I was able to celebrate with my family after seven years. We cooked the best goat meat, thanks to my mom’s famous recipe and some incredible Nepali spices.

I also did something special—after 10 years, I flew a kite. It was magical, and my wingman, Shishir, was a great help. I met my cousins after three years, and they made sure to braid my long hair (yes, I’ve been growing it for a year now). They even joked about me being their new girl cousin. I had the best braids, thanks to Sanshila and Sarisha, and of course, my mom’s stolen rubber bands!

I did a lot in Nepal this year. I visited Lakkha Cheen (a famous sweet shop), dressed up like a gangster, went to Basantapur and Boudha for the first time, and had an amazing time with Sujan and Unika. Speaking of Unika, thank you for enjoying world-famous Tibetan food with me. I know you wanted to eat everything, and I’m sorry I stopped you! 😒

Some congratulations are in order—one of my friends went exclusive, and while they want to remain anonymous, I’m happy for them. Another close friend also went exclusive, and while I know their partner well, I wish them nothing but the best in Chitwan!

Tihar was around the corner, and I made my own rangoli with diyas and colors. After the celebrations, we had our first family dinner, and everyone was ecstatic. It was great to meet so many people and celebrate together. I hope my being sick didn’t spoil the fun!

I returned to the U.S. and got a haircut—yes, there was popular demand. Seattle’s weather got even gloomier, but I liked it. I pranked another coworker who brought in a Christmas tree, and we had a good laugh about it. I went to Bainbridge Island, reconnecting with my love for photography, and took some amazing photos at Discovery Park. I also built my first keyboard and got my first pair of anti-blue light glasses. I look cool and feel nice!

As the year comes to a close, I visited Kashiv again, and he’s grown into a big boy! I want to end this year by wishing Kashiv a happy birthday and sending my best wishes for a happy new year to all my readers.
Here’s to 2025! 🎉
